title: Read-only multi-repo pull-request audit with a closure list

outcome.summary: A pure, read-only audit that turns per-repo `gh pr list --json` rows plus measured ancestry/patch-id facts into one normalised row per open pull request, assigns exactly one disposition per row (close-superseded, close-abandoned, keep-building, owner-decide), renders a markdown table, and returns a closure list of prepared close commands. The module never opens a socket, never runs a subprocess and never mutates a pull request; closures are strings the coordinator applies.
observable_behavior: `audit_rows(prs_by_repo, ancestry_by_repo, now_epoch=...)` returns one dict per open PR, sorted by (repo, number), carrying repo, number, title, branch, head, url, age_hours, updated_age_hours, draft, merge_state, ci_state, failing_checks, on_main, evidence and duplicate_of.
A head listed in `ancestor_heads` gets on_main true with evidence 'ancestor'; a head listed in `patch_matched_heads` gets on_main true with evidence 'patch-id'.

`dispositions(rows)` assigns close-superseded when the content is on main, close-abandoned for a later PR proposing the same head commit as an older one, keep-building for drafts, red CI, pending CI and BLOCKED/DIRTY merge states, and owner-decide for a green, mergeable PR that is not on main.

`build_report(...)` returns {rows, table, closures, counts} where table is markdown with a `| repo | pr |` header and closures is exactly one prepared `gh pr close <n> -R <repo> --comment "<reason>"` string per close row, in row order.
`python -m bundlebees_plugin.pr_audit --facts <json>` prints the report and exits 0; a missing, unreadable or malformed facts file exits 2 with a message on stderr.
An empty audit prints `0 open pull requests` and returns an empty closure list.

acceptance_criteria.statement: every open pull request yields exactly one normalised row, ordered by repo then number, with head, branch, url, age and CI fields populated
a head that is an ancestor of main is reported on_main with evidence ancestor and disposition close-superseded
a head whose patch already landed on main under another commit is reported with evidence patch-id and disposition close-superseded
a later open PR proposing the same head commit as an older open PR is close-abandoned with duplicate_of naming the older number
red CI keeps its failing check names and is keep-building, and a draft or BLOCKED/DIRTY merge state is keep-building even when every check is green
a green mergeable PR that is not on main is owner-decide, and a pending check is keep-building rather than green
the report renders a markdown table with a '| repo | pr |' header and exactly one prepared close command per close row

the module is read-only by construction: its own source carries no subprocess, socket, urllib, http.client or requests import and no prepared close or merge command literal outside the returned strings
the --facts entry point prints the report and exits 0, refuses a missing or malformed facts file with exit 2, and an empty audit says 0 open pull requests with no commands

dependencies: the facts (gh pr list --json rows, git merge-base --is-ancestor and patch-id results) are collected by the coordinator; this slice is a pure join
assumptions: the input rows are the subset of `gh pr list --json` the audit consumes; the collector is out of scope and may be a later slice
duplicate detection is same-head-commit within one repo; same-branch or same-title duplicates are not guessed at
the closure list is text for the coordinator to apply one command at a time after re-checking the evidence

authorized: read pull-request metadata in the coordinator-collected facts
write the spot-check table, the dispositions and the prepared closure list

reasons: one new read-only module on a source path; no dispatch, verify or merge surface
the closure list is advisory text, so a wrong disposition costs a review pass, not a mutation
the audit is the input to owner decisions about closing 20+ PRs, so the disposition rules are contract-bound
